# package storage

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/server/storage"
```

Package storage is the persistence boundary of the VTN. The server keeps no state of its own: everything goes through a Store.

Memory is the in-process implementation, for tests and for deployments that do not need to survive a restart.

## Variables

```go
var ErrCorrupt = errors.New("storage: the journal is corrupt")
```

ErrCorrupt reports a journal that cannot be replayed.

```go
var ErrReadOnly = errors.New("storage: the store is read-only")
```

ErrReadOnly is matched by every write to a File after one that could not be written to the journal: the store then accepts no change until it is opened again, so that memory is never more than one change ahead of the file. Reads go on.

## Functions

### func Decode

```go
func Decode[T Object](data []byte) (T, error)
```

Decode reads what Encode wrote.

### func Encode

```go
func Encode[T Object](v T) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns an object as JSON, for a Store that keeps its objects as documents, in a column of a database say. The types of package openadr have no JSON form of their own; this is the one the API gives them (OpenADR 3.1.0, as the VTN shows an object to its owner), and Decode reads it back to an equal value.

The form is stable: what one release of this module wrote, later ones read. It is the form storage.File writes to its journal.

### type Collection

```go
type Collection[T, F any] interface {
	// Create adds v. It returns a *ConstraintError if the ID is in use.
	Create(ctx context.Context, v T) error
	// Get returns the object with the given ID, or openadr.ErrNotFound.
	Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (T, error)
	// Update replaces the object that has v's ID, or returns
	// openadr.ErrNotFound.
	Update(ctx context.Context, v T) error
	// Delete removes and returns the object, or returns openadr.ErrNotFound.
	Delete(ctx context.Context, id string) (T, error)
	// List returns the objects that match every set field of filter, in the
	// order they were created.
	List(ctx context.Context, filter F) ([]T, error)
}
```

Collection stores objects of one type under their Metadata.ID, which the caller assigns.

Values are shared between the caller and the store: neither side modifies a value, or anything it points to, after handing it over.

### type File

```go
type File struct {

	// mu orders the writes: a change is applied to memory and appended to
	// the journal as one step, so that the journal replays to the same state.

}
```

File is a Store that survives a restart: it keeps everything in memory, like Memory, and writes every change to a journal file before the write returns. Opening the file replays the journal.

It is meant for a standalone VTN with a modest number of objects: all of them are held in memory, and the file is read in full at start. One process uses a file at a time; File does not lock it against a second.

A File is safe for concurrent use. Close it when done.

#### func OpenFile

```go
func OpenFile(path string, opts FileOptions) (*File, error)
```

OpenFile opens the store kept in the file at path, creating it when it does not exist. The journal is replayed and then rewritten without the changes that later ones made obsolete.

A last line that was cut short by a crash is dropped: the change it held had not been confirmed to anyone. Damage anywhere else is ErrCorrupt.

### type Outbox

```go
type Outbox interface {
	// AddDelivery records a notification that is to be delivered.
	AddDelivery(ctx context.Context, d Delivery) error
	// RemoveDelivery forgets one, because it was delivered or given up
	// on. Removing one that is not there is not an error.
	RemoveDelivery(ctx context.Context, id string) error
	// Deliveries returns those that are recorded, oldest first.
	Deliveries(ctx context.Context) ([]Delivery, error)
}
```

Outbox keeps the notifications a VTN has decided to send to webhooks until each has been delivered, so that a VTN that stops with notifications on their way sends them when it starts again. It is not part of Store: a VTN is given one with server.Config.Outbox, or does without. Memory and File are both a Store and an Outbox.

Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

### type Store

```go
type Store interface {
	Programs() Collection[openadr.Program, ProgramFilter]
	Events() Collection[openadr.Event, EventFilter]
	Reports() Collection[openadr.Report, ReportFilter]
	VENs() Collection[openadr.VEN, VENFilter]
	Resources() Collection[openadr.Resource, ResourceFilter]
	Subscriptions() Collection[SubscriptionRecord, SubscriptionFilter]
	// ResourceGroups holds what is not part of OpenADR 3.1.0; see
	// openadr.ResourceGroup. A store whose VTN does not serve resource
	// groups may return an empty collection that refuses every write.
	ResourceGroups() Collection[openadr.ResourceGroup, ResourceGroupFilter]
}
```

Store gives access to the collections of a VTN. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

A Store enforces what has to be decided atomically with a write:

  - program names and VEN names are unique, and so is a resource name within its VEN;
  - an event refers to an existing program, a report to an existing event, a resource to an existing VEN, and a subscription that names a program to an existing one;
  - a program that has events and a VEN that has resources cannot be deleted;
  - the children of a resource group exist, and a resource or resource group that is deleted leaves the groups it was a child of.

A violation is reported as a \*ConstraintError. Reports outlive the event they refer to.
